title: Derivation
description: A derivation's own declaration: src/main/<noun>/derivation.json (issues/1053). A derivation is a process whose two ends are files of the repository - it reads an upstream reference at one lineage and writes a schema family at that lineage's address - so the dev gate arbitrates it, where a pipeline, whose ends are the room's data, is arbitrated by the usr gate. Each path is repo-relative, with <lineage> standing for the declared lineage, so the lineage is said once.

lineage.description: The upstream lineage the derivation reads, as the reference names its directory: one of the lineages held under the reference project. The derivation takes it from here, never from which lineage is newest.

reads.description: The file the derivation is generated from, alone.

needs.description: What must stand for the derivation to run and is no input of its own: the generated parser its source is read through.

writes.description: What the derivation writes: first the schema family, at the lineage's address, then what it caches under tmp.

witness.description: The upstream file the family must agree with and is never generated from.

arbiter.description: The gate that arbitrates the process: the dev gate where both ends are committed files, the usr gate where they are the room's data.
